subject: Audit logging discovery / SOC 2 & exportability
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Audit logging discovery — recap & next steps

Thanks for the time this morning, Alice and Bob — good conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Summary of what we discussed:
- Scope: audit logging needs for Acme (admin activity, API request logs, exportability to S3 / long-term storage)
- Compliance drivers: SOC 2 proofpoints, GDPR data residency considerations, potential HIPAA impact for PHI flows
- Key asks from Acme: retention windows, immutability guarantees, log fields (request/response vs metadata), RBAC for log access, delivery/export options

Redwood answers / notes (high level):
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (2026) — I'll attach the report and the SOC summary.
- Audit logs: admin activity logs (user, action, resource, timestamp, IP, request id) + API logs (request id, endpoint, caller id, latency, token usage). We capture both metadata and request identifiers; we do not persist full request payloads by default unless configured for customer audits.
- Exportability: we support on-demand exports to S3 (server-side encrypted) and a scheduled export pipeline for longer retention. Exported objects can be versioned/immutable depending on the target storage options.
- Immutability: in-platform logs are append-only and retention-controlled; for long-term immutability we recommend exporting to a customer S3 bucket with object lock enabled.

Next steps / action items:
1) I will attach our audit logging overview + SOC 2 summary (attached).
2) Alice — please confirm which log fields are must-have vs nice-to-have and your preferred retention window.
3) We'll start a Vendor Security Questionnaire and loop in Rishi (security) and Monica (solutions) to help complete artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-audit-logging-overview.pdf (attachment)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logging discovery — recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) SOC 2: good to have the report. We have our procurement security review next week; SOC 2 Type II artifact will speed approvals.

2) Log fields: must-haves for us are:
   - Admin activity: actor, action, target resource, timestamp, IP, session id
   - API logs: request id, endpoint, caller id, response status, latency, token id (if available)

3) Retention: initial requirement is 1 year hot (searchable) and 7 years archived (cold). We may want immutability for the archived copy.

4) Export: Can you confirm whether exports can be pushed to our S3 with SSE-KMS and object-lock enabled? Also: do exported logs include the request/response bodies or only metadata?

5) Questionnaire: please send the vendor security questionnaire link and any place-holder artifacts; procurement will require the SOC 2 and the Audit Log schema.

If you can send the SOC 2 PDF and the logging schema today that would be perfect. I can schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week if we need to review details.

Best,
Alice

Head of Security Programs | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logging discovery — recap & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks. Answers inline and attachments included.

1) SOC 2: attached "redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf" and a SOC summary PDF. Let me know if procurement needs any additional attestation.

2) Log fields: Our default schemas include the fields you listed. For clarity:
   - Admin activity log entries: {actor_display, actor_email, action, resource_type, resource_id, timestamp_iso, ip_address, request_id, session_id, changed_fields} (we can export as JSON lines)
   - API logs: {request_id, caller_id, api_endpoint, http_method, status_code, latency_ms, bytes_in, bytes_out, token_hash, timestamp_iso}. We do not store full request bodies by default; for debugging customers can enable payload capture for a configurable short window (we recommend strict controls).

3) Retention & immutability:
   - In-platform: append-only store with configurable retention (30/90/365 days).
   - Exports: scheduled exports to your S3 (we support SSE-KMS) — if you enable S3 object-lock on your bucket the exported objects are immutable. We can also sign exports with a checksum and retention metadata.

4) Export mechanics: yes — we can push exports to a customer-owned S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and support object-lock. Exports are delivered as compressed NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) files partitioned daily.

5) Attachments + questionnaire: starting the vendor security questionnaire now — link below. I've attached the audit logging overview and the SOC 2 report. Also attaching a small logging schema spreadsheet for procurement.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-report-2026.pdf; audit-logging-tech-spec.xlsx; redwood-audit-logging-overview.pdf

If it helps, we can do a technical deep-dive with Rishi (security) and Monica (solutions) this week. When's a good time?

Thanks,
Marissa
